title: "Now from the Roaring Lion's Rage
description: "Now from the Roaring Lion's Rage in Tonic Solfa to ST. FLAVIAN, doh is F: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 6 verses and a piano.
about: Isaac Watts wrote these words for The Psalms of David Imitated in the Language of the New Testament (1719): Psalm 22, part 2, headed “Christ's sufferings and kingdom”.
Watts' psalms were printed without tunes and sung to any tune of their metre, Common Metre (8.6.8.6). This page sets the words to ST. FLAVIAN; any other Common Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: "Now from the roar-ing li-on's rage, "O Lord, pro-tect thy Son; "Nor leave thy dar-ling to en-gage, "The powers of hell a-lone."

lines: Thus did our suffering Saviour pray,
God heard him in that dreadful day,
Great was the victory of his death,
And all the kindreds of the earth
They shall be reckon'd in his eyes
The meek and humble soul shall see
And all that seek the Lord shall be
The isles shall know the righteousness

source: Isaac Watts, The Psalms of David Imitated (1719)
licence: Public domain: Isaac Watts died in 1748.
credits: Words by Isaac Watts (1674–1748), public domain; set to ST. FLAVIAN by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
